posts.headline: Iraq's Communications and Media Commission cancels Korek Telecom settlement
posts.summary: Kurdistan Watch flags the CMC's cancellation of its settlement with Korek Telecom over unpaid debts of roughly 1.4 trillion Iraqi dinars, warning the move could freeze the KDP-linked operator's commercial footing.

posts.headline: Public clash over KRG non-oil revenue figures between Finance Minister and Halwest leader
posts.summary: The KRG Finance Minister puts monthly non-oil revenue at about 100 billion Iraqi dinars while a Halwest Movement leader counters that actual receipts exceed 400 billion a month, reopening the regional fiscal-transparency question.

posts.headline: After Bahrain, Kuwait and UAE also shut their airspace
posts.summary: Kuwait and the UAE follow Bahrain in closing their airspace amid the fresh Iranian salvo and CENTCOM strikes on Qeshm, expanding the Gulf-wide aviation shutdown overnight. Translated from Arabic.

posts.headline: Coverage of Iranian drone attempts and US airstrikes on Qeshm Island
posts.summary: AMrym tracks the Iranian drone attempts against US assets in the Gulf and the parallel CENTCOM self-defence strikes on an IRGC ground-control station on Qeshm Island, the operational anchor of the current escalation wave. Translated from Arabic.

posts.headline: Extended take on Coordination Framework pressures and American demands on Baghdad
posts.summary: AMrym lays out the live pressure on the Coordination Framework from Washington over the arms-monopoly file, slotting the AAH and Imam Ali handover moves inside an American conditionality framework on Baghdad. Translated from Arabic.

posts.headline: Sardonic read that the latest disarmament gesture is principled self-disarmament rather than a binding handover
posts.summary: Mike Knight takes a wry view of the militia leader's disarmament posture, suggesting the US Government should send a congratulatory note rather than treat the announcement as a genuine state-monopoly delivery.

posts.headline: All three Iraqi groups that have pledged to disarm are inside the Sadrist trend
posts.summary: Knight notes that the three groups that have publicly pledged disarmament so far in Iraq all sit inside the Sadrist political and ideological orbit, flagging that the Iran-aligned core has not yet credibly moved on the arms-monopoly file.
